In Australia, the S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.4pc to 9,155.80.

Data from the US on Wednesday showed consumer prices had risen in line with analysts’ expectations in July.

Wall Street stocks were boosted on Wednesday by gains made by tech companies CoreWeave and Super Micro Computer, both of which closed up by more than 19pc.

The Nasdaq Composite ended the session up 0.5pc, with the S&P 500 up nearly 0.3pc. The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished the session marginally down.

Oil prices were little changed as investors weighed the deadlock in talks between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, was broadly flat at nearly $89 a barrel.

News.title: H5N1 sparks a very Australian epidemic
News.content:
H5N1 bird flu has reached Australia’s shores and is threatening to infect some of the country’s most unique wildlife.

Australasia is the last continent to be hit by the highly infectious avian influenza H5N1, a new strain of which has been circulating worldwide since 2020.

Since recording its first case in June, more than 200 wild seabirds in Australia have been infected, with fears that the highly infectious flu could quickly ‘jump’ to other species.

While H5N1 has infected animals from foxes to sea lions in other parts of the world in recent years, the epidemic now threatens some of Australia’s most iconic wildlife – many of which are found nowhere else on earth.

An Australian government assessment of more than 2,000 native species warned that nearly one in five faces a high risk from the deadly H5N1 bird flu, with hundreds of unique birds and mammals vulnerable to severe population reductions or even extinction.

Those animals include iconic species like the Tasmanian devils, quolls, and dingoes.

Other aquatic mammals, including the platypus, which is only found in Australia, are at risk of infection through contact with bird droppings in shared wetlands and coastal environments.

News.title: Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end
News.content:
Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

News.title: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG
News.content:
His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

News.title: Advice, cookbooks and emergency pot noodles: Your best gifts for university students
News.content:
When it comes to sending a child or grandchild off to university, it can be tempting to fill their room with every conceivable gadget.

So to help, we asked the Telegraph Recommended Community for their best gift recommendations and their suggestions ranged from desk lamps to cookery books and supermarket gift cards.

Here are the essentials worth buying.

Kitchen basics

From cupboard essentials to electrical appliances and cookbooks, most readers say they’d gift kitchen equipment.

Thinking back to his university days, reader TJ, 43, from London, says “the main essentials are around kitchen items and good long lasting food”.

“It’s nice to have some bits to cook for others as well and to make friends quickly,” he adds.

Susan, 54, from the West Midlands, agrees, recommending “basic cooking equipment” as a key staple and “distinctive cutlery, plates and cups that are easily identified”, which are particularly useful for shared accommodation.

“A box of store cupboard ingredients such as olive oil, soy, stock cubes and spices to use when cooking,” is also well-received, she says.

News.title: Ebola outbreak ‘doubling every 20 days’, warns UN chief
News.content:
Congo’s runaway Ebola outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days, according to the United Nations humanitarian chief, putting it on track to soon be the largest ever seen.

Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the case load is expanding exponentially and many believe the true toll is far higher than recorded.

If cases continue to double at the same rate, the flare-up in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will surpass the record West African outbreak sometime around the end of September.

Modelling by one health analytics firm already predicts there is a more than 90 per cent chance that the DRC will become the largest on record.

The two-year West African outbreak grew to more than 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths across Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea from late 2013 to 2016.

This year’s outbreak centred on the DRC province of Ituri has already seen 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths in only a few months.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

Sports.title: Man Utd new-boy Youri Tielemans shares statement APOLOGISING after being accused of ‘offending’ and ‘undermining’ Villa
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED star Youri Tielemans has apologised to Aston Villa after claiming his new club were “above” them.

The Belgium midfielder, 29, sealed a £35million switch to Old Trafford after the Red Devils paid his release clause.



But Tielemans ruffled a few feathers after admitting United were one of the clubs bigger than Villa.

He said: “I am very thankful to Aston Villa. I owe them the world. It is a great club, we did amazing things, and they have put me back to my best level.



“But there are clubs above Villa, and Manchester United is one of them.”

His words didn’t go down well with some Villa supporters as some asked if the jibe was “necessary”.



And he put out an apology for Villa fans after the “mistake” of his “choice of words”.

He wrote on his Instagram story: “Never meant for my words in the press yesterday to offend anyone or undermine the institution of Aston Villa Football Club, which I massively respect and I’m grateful to for the past 3 years.

“I must however admit my mistake and apologise for my choice of words, will be more careful in the future.

“Wishing the club the best in the future. Youri.”

Sports.title: Italy ‘to hand shock national team debut to highly-rated teen striker wanted by Brazil’
Sports.content:
ITALY could be set to hand a competitive debut to highly-rated youngster Samuele Inacio to fend off interest from Brazil.

Inacio, 18, is a Borussia Dortmund starlet who is beginning to make waves since making his first-team debut last season.



Born in Bergamo, Italy, to a Brazilian father playing in Serie A at the time, Inacio is eligible to play for either nation.

So far in his career he has chosen the country of his birth, being capped at a number of age groups in Italy’s youth system.



He even made his senior debut earlier this year in a friendly against Luxembourg.

But Brazil scouts are said to be circling, given that the youngster is free to change allegiances until he makes his first competitive appearance for either country.



Gianluca DiMarzio reported that the national team, currently fronted by Carlo Ancelotti, sent scouts to watch Inacio as Dortmund took on Arsenal in a pre-season friendly at the weekend.

They watched him open the scoring against the Premier League champions just seven minutes into the contest, helping his side to an eventual 3-2 win.

The Italian football insider went on to suggest Italy under new manager Roberto Mancini are eager to lock the starlet down before his head can be turned.

They could even cap him at the earliest opportunity, the September international break, to commit his future to Italy, where reports say his loyalties still lie for the time being.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea MUST sign Emi Martinez from Aston Villa in rival transfer swoop to become genuine title contenders
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are a top-level goalkeeper away from challenging for the Premier League title, and there is one they should be targeting.

The Blues have spent very well this summer, buying players with Premier League experience who are ready to make the step up to competing for the biggest titles, having shone individually with their former clubs.



The likes of Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers are the best two examples of players from within the league who could infinitely improve in the right environment and become some of the best in the league in their positions.

Look at Joao Pedro, Moises Caicedo, and even Marc Cucurella – Chelsea, when buying from within the Premier League, have a good hit rate of their players becoming top tier.



Of course, in their goalkeeper – Robert Sanchez – they already tried this once.

So what they need to do in goal is not sign someone and hope they will improve, it’s to sign someone who is already world-class.



That someone is Emiliano Martinez of Aston Villa.

I mean, you’ve already taken their most creative player and their set-piece coach – surely Behdad Eghbali could have set up some sort of Buy two get one free deal, no?

The dilemma with Sanchez is, that he’s not that bad.

He is not bad enough that the club desperately need a new goalkeeper because he is constantly throwing the ball in his own net or making stupid errors and not making saves.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Actually he is a fairly solid Premier League keeper – but fairly solid is not going to win you titles.

He is a good shot stopper, who is okay with his feet, and improves drastically when he is playing with confidence, which was personified when Chelsea won the Club World Cup and he genuinely looked like one of the world’s best keepers.

So if Xabi Alonso can instill that level of confidence in him again, then maybe Chelsea will back themselves to win the league with him in between the posts.

That said, they would certainly back themselves a little more if they had a world-class keeper, who has won the World Cup, the Europa League with Villa, and back-to-back Yashin Trophies with several years of Premier League experience as one of the league’s best stoppers.

Not only that, but Martinez just feels so Chelsea – he is the kind of s******** personality that Stamford Bridge would fall in love with.



So why are Chelsea not going out and getting him?

Well firstly, as I said, Sanchez is not THAT bad, or bad enough that the club are desperate to replace him, not in the same way that they needed a centre-back or a left-winger.

The club are happy with their goalkeeping options, including the supposed next best goalkeeper in the world in Mike Penders.

So much so that there is no interest in signing the likes of Diogo Costa from Porto, despite an appreciation of his ability.



They did look into the signing of Mike Maignan from AC Milan last summer as a market opportunity, but the deal couldn’t be made and he signed a new contract in Milan.

Other keepers that they could look into signing, that would be an improvement on Sanchez, include Borussia Dortmund‘s Gregor Kobel, Spain‘s number one Unai Simon, or Roma‘s Mile Svilar.

Maignan and even someone like Jan Oblak from Atletico Madrid could be good options too.

It feels though, as if Chelsea will go into this season with Sanchez as the number one and Penders as the number two, with the Belgian at some point being given a chance to stake his claim in the first team early.

The Spaniard feels like he has Alonso’s backing this term, and claimed that his countryman’s ‘simplicity’ will benefit him, after sometimes struggling to cope with the complexities of playing the goalkeeper role under Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior.



Sanchez said on Alonso: “It is the simplification of things.

“He is allowing me to do what I am best at. I have already played a lot of games in the Premier League and people know what I am good at or not.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“He is allowing me to do what I do best and that means my confidence is going to be boosted and I am going to play better and better. That is what is great about him.”



If things are not so simple by January though, Chelsea could be looking to dip into the goalkeeper market mid-season once more.

Sports.title: Every Premier League kit ranked ahead of 2026/27 season with ‘Teletubby’ shirt tanking and Arsenal missing top spot
Sports.content:
THE new Premier League season is almost here, which means it’s also time to rate and slate every kit for the 2026-27 campaign.

New shirts often generate nearly as much debate as transfers.

And it’s fair to say some clubs have been savaged over their threads this year.



So we’ve decided to jump on the bandwagon and give our own verdict over the latest designs.



Here is SunSport’s official ranking of all 20 Premier League home kits.

20 – Hull City

Starting us off in last place is newly-promoted Hull City, who have come out with, in my humble opinion, an absolute howler of a home kit that looks more like a rugby jersey.

The Tigers have ditched last season’s one-colour body in favour of retro black and orange stripes, but they’ve got a bizarre new logo featuring just the letters HCAFC, which definitely looks odd.



They’ve also got a new kit supplier Oxen – which replaces Kappa – and a new white collar has come in to match the same colour on the sleeves.

Worth a try? If you like rugby, maybe…

Despite our verdict, it appears to have sold out at the club shop, proving we know nothing. The rather tastsy away shirt is available though…



19 – Newcastle

Less a football kit, more an optical illusion. Some fans have dubbed it “the barcode kit” with what the club calls a “bold, disrupted stripe pattern”.

It’s certainly bold, alright, but not in a good way. Gone are Newcastle’s traditional thick black and white stripes in favour of… whatever this is.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

There’s a series of vertical stripes varying in size that spread to the sleeves – with a thick light blue pattern on the shoulder.

It just doesn’t really work and it seems fans agree.



18 – Bournemouth

The tragic thing about Bournemouth’s new home shirt is that it MIGHT have been OK if it didn’t have a giant pink Vitality logo spread across the middle of a black and red striped shirt.

The only problem is: It DOES have a giant pink Vitality logo spread across the middle of a black and red striped shirt. Some have even compared it to something out of the Teletubbies. It’s a shame as well because I like the gold detail on the collarbone.

But the placement, size and colour of the sponsor just absolutely wrecks this kit – which is a shame as it’s Bournemouth’s first season in Europe. Sorry, Cherries.

17 – Leeds

Have you ever spilt sauce down your crisp white T-shirt and tried to wash it out, but you could still see stain left behind? That’s what Leeds’ new kit looks like to me.



The issue is the interesting choice of horizontal blue and yellow pinstripes running aross the body. Yellow and white is always a big no-no when it comes to football kits, for me anyway.

But here the yellow stripes just look messy from afar. I do like the yellow and blue detail around the collar and the blue on the shoulders and sleeves. But the main part of the design is an eyesore. At the very least, maybe it will distract Leeds’ opponents this season.

16 – Crystal Palace

Never been a fan of a seat belt kit and that’s exactly what Palace have done here – moving away from the traditional blue/red combination for the first time since the 2008-09 season.

Instead, the blue/red colours are on the diagonal sash and a similar pattern is seen running across the sleeves too. It actually looks closer to last season’s away kit and doesn’t really feel like a home kit.



Kit sponsor Temporal is also a new addition, as is a re-imagined version of the club crest. Unfortunately it’s just not as strong as recent Palace kits.

15 – Nottingham Forest

What’s this? The first Premier League kit to use tie-dye for their design? No, that’s not happening, but it certainly looks like it.

Forest manufacturers Adidas have gone for a striking all red strip with dark patches blotched all over. It’s a bit of a mess and definitely a downgrade on their elegant 2025-26 kit with white pinstripes.

The simple white stripes on the shoulders are nice but the rest is just too much to look at.



14 – Chelsea

Chelsea‘s new home kit looks simple and decent – until you squint your eyes and realise a giant version of the club’s badge has been imprinted on the body of the shirt.

This might have been a classy, subtle detail if the crest features were much smaller and woven into the fabric. But the whole crest is plastered straight on to the front and the fact there is no kit sponsor draws more attention to it.

I am a fan of the collar and contrast of blue and yellow, plus the nice little yellow slashes on the shoulders. If they get a new front of shirt sponsor this instantly gets elevated a few places.



13 – Everton

Not a bad entry from Everton and an improvement on last year’s home kit that had black horizontal zigzags running through it.

New sponsor CMC Markets has entered the chat in the third shirt designed by Castore. There’s also yellow edge to the white collar and a patch of orange on the sleeve which helps it stand out.

It’s playing it pretty safe so I’m putting it at 13th, which is where Everton finished last season.

12 – Coventry

Safe to say Coventry’s new home strip hasn’t gone down too well with fans. Some have claimed it looks too similar to Sheffield Wednesday.



No doubt, the shirt they wore during their promotion-winning campaign of 2025-26 was much cleaner with an all sky blue colour. This year the club have brought back the blue and white stripes.

I don’t think it’s too bad but the orange Monzo logo running across it doesn’t look great.

11 – Fulham

Another club that has switched out its shirt sponsor as Fulham trades SBO Top for ClickHouse and goes for a black, white and red theme.

It’s a pretty fine kit that doesn’t try to do anything tricky or complicated. Fans have got a neat and simple design that’s pleasing to the eye.



And that’s why it’s in the middle of the range in our rankings.

10 – Ipswich

Not too dissimilar to last season, the Tractor Boys have produced another clean dark blue design with the same Halo front of sponsor logo.

But what shines from this kit is the diamond-shaped pattern across the body of the shirt.

It does the job and it’s nice and tidy. I wish the same could be said about their away shirt – the less said about that, the better.



9 – Brighton

Brighton shirts usually look more or less the same every year. It’s normally a variation of blue and white vertical stripes, so no surprises for guessing they have another variety this season.

I have to say though, I am a fan of the smaller stripes, which have been squeezed into white pinstripes, with a white v-neck at the top.

Brighton are often credited for their stylish performances and consistency and they’re doing the same thing with their kit this season.



8 – Aston Villa

The reigning Europa League champions have gone a shade darker on the burgundy and got rid of the light-blue sleeves, and this is a really nice effort from Adidas.

The blue colour has transitioned to the sleeve and shoulder with a classy new collar.

There’s also a new shirt sponsor with Visit Rwanda replacing Betano for this season. All round it’s a solid entry for the Villans.

7 – Tottenham

Nike have been accused of playing it safe too often with their Tottenham designs – and this season’s kit won’t do anything to change that view.



But what you can’t argue with is that they’ve come up with a nice, clean design that won’t cause too many complaints. There’s a faint diagonal grey striped pattern cutting across the body that helps it stand out.

And the manufacturers have included navy streaks down the sides of the kit, with a unique, layered design of the neck. It scores points for cleanliness but loses points for lack of edginess.

6 – Man City

A new era for the Sky Blues after Pep Guardiola ended his 10-year reign at the Etihad and City have a new kit to match that feels reminiscent of their older editions.

It’s pure light blue all over with a gradient at the bottom that fades it ever so slightly.



There is white trim on the neckline and edges of the sleeves, which makes it look similar to the 2009-10 kit. It will please the purists as the logos are all the same colour, creating a great contrast to the light blue.

5 – Sunderland

I do love it when a club pays homage to a classic kit and that’s exactly what Sunderland have done with their new home shirt.

The Black Cats have come out with what is probably the most visually striking and unique design that is influenced by their 1937 FA Cup-winning kit.

The vintage-style shirt keeps the thick red and white vertical stripes but introduces a pointy collar with the club’s logo protected by an old-school crest. It’s an instant classic as Sunderland play a first season in the Europa League.



4 – Man United

If we were ranking away kits, United would be first place on this list. But their home strip is pretty good too – another clean design with a collar.

The all-red shirt is lovely with a small but eye-catching black and white strip pattern on the collar and sleeve.

It looks like a classic Manchester United shirt design with the Snapdragon logo in white down the front. You won’t get too many complaints about this at all as United prepare for their first full season under Michael Carrick.



3 – Arsenal

They’re the reigning Premier League champions but they don’t quite top the standings on this list, unfortunately.

That’s not to say Arsenal don’t have a very nice looking kit, however, quite the opposite. It feels like an evolution from their title-winning kit as dark stripes are added to the shoulder.

And on the edges of the sleeve and neckline you can see a small red and black pattern that gives it a standout effect.

2 – Liverpool

One of the more ‘out there’ design choices from Adidas, who have created a unique strip that has a firework-style pattern.



The red shirt has little white triangles and lines dotted around that looks like it’s exploding across the kit.

There’s also a red edge around the neckline and white stripes on the shoulder (as seen on many Adidas designs). It’s eye-catching and scores points for bravery.

1 – Brentford

The Bees will be buzzing with this design from Joma – not just because it’s sleek, bold and punchy.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Brentford announced that this will be their kit for the next TWO seasons, which should help avoid fans having to pay obscene prices year after year. Fans across the Prem should have little to critique on this kit and it’s had rave reviews across the board.



Joma have kept things simple with the red and white stripes – but what brings it together are the yellow and black detail around the neckline, sleeves and sides of the kit. It makes the whole thing look eye-popping and it’s the winner for me.

Sports.title: Why Bruno Fernandes is the most expensive midfielder in Dream Team this season — and gaffers are willing to pay!
Sports.content:
ONLY Erling Haaland (£8.5m) is more expensive than Bruno Fernandes (£7m) ahead of the new Dream Team season.

Given Manchester City’s No9 is clearly in a bracket of his own as the only player to amass to 400+ points last season, Manchester United’s captain has been bestowed a lofty status ahead of Gameweek 1.

PLAY DREAM TEAM NOW: £100,000 PRIZE POT!



Fernandes’ punchy price tag may come as a surprise to some managers as he finished joint-sixth among midfielders in 2025/26.



In fact, Dominik Szoboszlai (£6m), the reigning leader in his position, outperformed the Portuguese playmaker by 53 points.

So why is the Liverpool man a full £1million cheaper?

One only needs to dig a little deeper into the numbers to understand why gaffers will have to part with such a substantial portion of their budget if they want to own Fernandes from the get-go.



Last term’s return of nine goals (three of them penalties) was modest but the 31-year-old broke new ground when it came to assisting his team-mates.

Fernandes broke the official Premier League record for most assists in a campaign, ending with 21 to his name to eclipse the best efforts of Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne.

In Dream Team, with Opta-defined ‘fantasy assists’ and other competitions included, he registered 25 assists when all was said and done.

His closest competitor in the metric, Rayan Cherki (£5m), finished on 18 assists.



Fernandes was also in a league of his own for big chances created, proof that he was worthy of his unrivalled assist total.

The supremacy of United’s No8 was particularly impressive given the Red Devils fulfilled the fewest fixtures possible last season.

By way of a comparison, Arsenal played 63 games.

Fernandes averaged 8.1 points-per-game in 2025/26 on his way to a total of 300 — no other midfielder averaged more than seven points-per-game.

Whether he’s able to produce the goods again is another conversation but his record over six and a half seasons at Old Trafford is outstanding.

Sports.title: Chelsea ‘land transfer pay-day windfall’ as Romelu Lukaku completes stunning Fenerbahce move from Napoli
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are set to bank a transfer windfall after Romelu Lukaku completed his move from Napoli to Fenerbahce.

The Turkish giants have snapped up the Belgium striker in a deal that will see the Blues benefit thanks to a sell-on clause inserted when they allowed Lukaku to join Napoli two years ago.



The exact transfer fee has not been disclosed, but the Stamford Bridge club are in line for a welcome financial boost from the sale of the 33-year-old.

Lukaku endured an injury-hit campaign last season, making just seven appearances in all competitions for Napoli, but he still managed to add to his reputation as one of Belgium’s greatest-ever forwards by scoring three goals at the World Cup.



The striker, Belgium’s record goalscorer with 93, has now returned to Turkey, a country close to his heart after spending part of his childhood there when his father Roger played for Super Lig side Genclerbirligi.

In a message to Fenerbahce supporters, Lukaku said: “It’s an honour and a privilege to be joining your club.

“I am fit, 100 per cent, ready to go. It is an emotional moment after many years to be going back to Turkey where I lived as a young kid, where I discovered the professional world as a toddler with my dad.”

Lukaku leaves Napoli having won the Serie A title and adds Fenerbahce to a career that has also seen him lift league crowns with Anderlecht and Inter Milan, as well as the Club World Cup with Chelsea.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The move makes him the second former Manchester United forward to join Fenerbahce this summer after Mason Greenwood’s arrival from Marseille.



Fenerbahce, who have finished runners-up to Galatasaray in each of the last four seasons, are chasing their first Turkish league title since 2014, and will hope Lukaku can fire them back to the top.

For Chelsea, the deal provides another boost to their transfer strategy, with the club continuing to benefit from smart clauses included in previous player sales.

Sports.title: Celtic sign midfielder Baur on an initial four-year deal
Sports.content:
Celtic have made their fourth summer signing with midfielder Mika Baur joining on an initial four-year deal, with the option for a further year.

The 22-year-old arrives in a deal worth around £6.8m, joining from German club Paderborn, after helping them win promotion from the second tier of German football to the Bundesliga.

He scored four times and provided five assists across 33 league appearances last season, and was named the club's player of the year.

Sky Sports News understand the Scottish champions will pay an initial fee of around £4.5m for Baur, with £2.3m in add-ons making up the deal.

Similar to deals struck with fellow summer signings Camilo Duran, Kasper Høgh and Haissem Hassan, a large proportion of the bonuses will be paid out if Celtic reach the league phase of the Champions League.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Summer signing Kasper Hogh scored a hat-trick in just his second league game at Celtic

Celtic face LASK Linz in their play-off tie next week, and Baur - who came through the youth ranks at Freiburg before moving to Paderborn in 2024 - could now be registered for that Champions League squad.

On joining the Scottish Champions, Baur said: "It's absolutely the right move.

"It's a great club and I've heard incredible things about the fans.

"I'm in the same agency as Nicolas Kuhn so I called him to ask a couple of questions and he was so positive. He said, if you have the chance, just do it.

"I've had a good pre-season with good matches and tough training sessions, everything. So I'm in good shape and I'm ready to go."

Sports.title: Richards to face Kalajdzic showdown on Fisher bill
Sports.content:
British former world title challenger Craig Richards will take on Radivoje Kalajdzic in a 10-round light heavyweight showdown, while Lee Cutler faces Louis Greene in a middleweight clash, on Zuffa Boxing's Johnny Fisher bill at London's Copper Box Arena.

Richards vs Kalajdzic will serve as the chief support bout to the 10-round heavyweight main event featuring Fisher at Zuffa Boxing 11 on September 26, live on Sky Sports.

An opponent for 'The Romford Bull' will be announced in the coming days.

Richards (20-4-1, 13 KOs) is a world-ranked former British champion who fought Dmitry Bivol for the WBA light-heavyweight title in 2021. He won his two most recent fights in 2025, including a knockout win over Dan Azeez last December.

The fight will mark the first time hard-hitting, Serbian-born Kalajdzic (30-3, 22 KOs) has fought outside North America as a professional. The 35-year-old's last fight was a seventh-round knockout victory against Oleksandr Gvozdyk in February.

The Copper Box Arena bill will also feature a 10-round middleweight showdown between British boxers Cutler and Greene.

Cutler beat Stevie McKenna on points when they fought in December 2024, marking the only professional defeat for Ireland's KO king so far.

Image: Lee Cutler and Louis Greene clash at middleweight

Cutler's last fight saw him stop Aaron Sutton in his hometown of Bournemouth in three rounds, while Greene - a former Commonwealth super-welterweight champion - earned a points decision win over Daniel Buciuc in Dublin last week.

Decorated British amateur Kayla Allen is also fighting as part of her professional debut after becoming the first female fighter to sign with Zuffa Boxing.

Alex MacMillan, Leon Hughes and Fred Pullen, who is also turning professional, are also on the London bill.

Watch Johnny Fisher's next fight at London's Copper Box Arena, on Saturday September 26, live on Sky Sports. Get Sky Sports or stream boxing with no contract.

Sports.title: Atherton: 'England must become Root's team - he has a unique opportunity'
Sports.content:
Fresh from exclusively speaking to Joe Root following his reappointment as England captain, Sky Sports Cricket's Michael Atherton looks further into the move...

Sitting down with Joe Root, he seemed pretty relaxed, optimistic and excited about taking on the captaincy for a second time.

And there's a fundamental reason for that, I suppose. How many of us in life get a second chance at something?

When you're made captain or you lead an organisation, people always say: 'Make sure you do it your way and don't have any regrets at the end of it because you won't get another go at this.'

Joe Root is getting another go at it.

The key points from Joe Root's interview Root rules out curfew despite ECB guidelines and tells players to "be adults" when using alcohol

The England captain was "gutted" at the departure of former England Test head coach McCullum departure but has reasserted his excitement for a new era with incoming coach Stephen Fleming, who he admires

Root admits to "over-bowling" Jofra Archer during his first spell as captain but has vowed to protect England's "generational talent" this time around

Root has refused to rule out a return for Ben Stokes for the 2027 Ashes

How many of us would love to retrace our steps and have another go at something that we did well or not so well the first time around? He's got that opportunity now.

He's got a chance to bring all his wisdom and his knowledge and perhaps right some of the mistakes he made first time around.

I mean, he had a good time of it as England captain. Nobody has won more games in the role; equally, nobody has lost as many, so it wasn't a completely smooth ride for him.

The hope is that he can bring a lot of that knowledge and wisdom to bear the second time around.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Root gives his first interview since being reappointed England Test captain

He will want to do it a little bit differently, because you've got to think that between his first coming and his second coming as captain, there's been four years of Ben Stokes and Brendon McCullum driving an England team to play in a way that probably no other England team in the history of the game has played.

Root is coming in on the back of that.

A lot of our interview is about how he wants to keep certain things of Bazball - if you want to call it that - but also tweak some things and put his own stamp on it.

This has now got to be Root's team again, not Stokes' team. So the transition to that will be a fascinating one.

'Captaincy won't affect Root like last time, nor his batting'

I asked him whether it was out of a desire to do it or a duty because there are very few other options.

You have to remember that when he gave up the captaincy the first time around, he talked about having an unhealthy relationship with it, so I put a couple of questions about that to him.

Is he certain he won't be damaged by the captaincy again? A lot of the answers revolve around the COVID years.

He had to lead England during a couple of COVID years, and he felt that had a particular negative impact on him.

Of course, it is a very different time now.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking after the New Zealand Test win in 2022, Root explained why he'd taken the decision to step-away from Test captaincy

And I'm confident the pressures of captaincy won't impact how he performs with the bat. It didn't the first time around.

Although in the interview he says he felt it impacted him initially, he actually felt that, in the last year or 18 months of his captaincy, he was batting as well as ever. The numbers suggest he did pretty well as a batting captain; I think he averaged 46 during that time.

The biggest line is about the curfew, which we put out there. And I'm very happy that he's done that.

Curfews are a crazy way to run a grown-up, professional sporting team. I'm very glad that, between him and new Test coach Stephen Fleming, they've sat down and said: 'Let's treat these players as grown-ups.'

If they step out of line and mess up, there is going to be consequences. Your expectations have to be clear to the players, but treat people like grown-ups.

Sports.title: Australia exposed by Bangladesh in stunning start to first Test
Sports.content:
Bangladesh's bowlers overshadowed Australia's Big Four getting back together on day one of the first Test as the hosts were dismissed for 198 and Hasan Mahmud took a career-best 6-55.

Bangladesh's top-order batters then combined to reach 96-1 at stumps and cut the first-innings deficit to 102.

Bangladesh lost their last Test match against Zimbabwe in June by an innings and 85 runs but in Darwin on Thursday made a dream start to their tour of Australia, where they are playing their first Test series since 2003.

Australia are beginning a schedule of at least 20 Tests over the coming 12 months, with tours of New Zealand, South Africa, India and England - where The Ashes begins at Trent Bridge from June 18. Steve Smith admitted their start against Bangladesh was "not our best"

"Still plenty of cricket to be played, obviously," Smith added.

"It would have been nice to have taken a few more [wickets]. So, hopefully we start ⁠well in the morning, pick up a few early ones and ⁠put pressure on."

Mahmud starred for the visitors with consistent line and length, striking in his sixth and seventh overs to remove openers Jake Weatherald (23) and Travis Head (22) after Australia won the toss and raced to 45 without loss on a green-tinged pitch.

Image: Bangladesh's Hasan Mahmud made the difference with the ball on day one

From there, Mahmud and fellow pacemen Taskin Ahmed (2-55) and Ebadot Hossain (2-39) dominated the first two sessions, bowling with discipline to exploit the conditions and get on top of a batting line-up that was held together primarily by Smith's defiant 71.

Smith was the next-to-last wicket to fall, advancing at Mahmud before top-edging a high catch to wicketkeeper Litton Das, bringing an innings featuring seven boundaries and a six to an end.

The day started positively for the hosts, with skipper Pat Cummins winning the toss. Playing just his second Test in 13 months, he reunited with fellow pacemen Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc and veteran off-spinner Nathan Lyon in a frontline attack long known in Australia as the Big Four.

A partisan crowd was in full support of Darwin-born Weatherald but he never really settled and needlessly swiped at a ball from Mahmud. Head was out soon after, chopping on a delivery that was bowled from around the wicket as Australia slipped to 52-2.

Ebadot had Marnus Labuschagne (1) caught by Bangladesh skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto, and could have dismissed Smith early too, but a chance at third slip was put down.

Ebadot dismissed Alex Carey (19) after the break and Taskin bowled Beau Webster (12).

Hasan had Cummins (9) and Starc (1) out edging and wrapped up the innings in 53 overs with the wickets of Smith and Lyon.

Despite having their first-choice bowling attack back together, Australia were unable to take more than one Bangladesh wicket, with Mominul Haque (35) and Tanzid Hasan (32) going on to share an unbeaten 60-run stand.

'Opportunity here that may have been missed' - Ponting questions Australia selectors

Speaking to Australia's Channel 7, former captain Ricky Ponting said: "Look, what's the state of Australian cricket?

"This has been a very, very successful cricket team. (But) right now, there are a couple of chinks in the armour and the selectors decided to stick with what they know.

"At the end of last season, I thought the time was right now to blood a couple of youngsters into these two Test matches. I said (Campbell) Kellaway and (Ollie) Peake were the ones that I wanted to have.

"So they decided not to do that. But my worry is, when do they do that? Are you going to debut these guys in South Africa against (Kagiso) Rabada and (Marco) Jansen and co?

"I think that would be a whole lot harder. So I just feel there's an opportunity here that may have been missed."

Sports.title: Could UK diaspora players represent India? | Bhatia closes in on Liverpool stake
Sports.content:
Welcome to Dev's Digest, a regular Sky Sports column in which Asian Football Award winner Dev Trehan delivers exclusive news and reflects on some of the key developments for British South Asians in Football.

Indian football chiefs are increasingly confident that diaspora footballers from Britain will be allowed to play for the national team, Sky Sports News can exclusively reveal.

Current rules prevent Indian-heritage footballers abroad from playing for the national side unless they surrender their overseas passport.

That has prevented British Indians from earning international recognition and the opportunity to help India break back into the world's top 100 FIFA-ranked nations.

But one senior official has told Sky Sports News he is "convinced" the path will be cleared to allow eligible overseas footballers to represent India.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After the All India Football Federation set up a task force to assess the status of players of Indian origin who could represent the national team, Arunava Chaudhuri told Sky Sports News’ Dev Trehan he thinks four or five British Indian lads could get into the squad

Reacting exclusively to Sky Sports News, former Mumbai City FC chief operating officer Arunava Chaudhuri said: "We are closer than we've ever been to seeing Overseas Citizens of India representing the Blue Tigers.

"Diaspora footballers from Europe can take the Indian team to another level.

"We're now talking about something that potentially extends beyond football, with the next Commonwealth Games coming to Ahmedabad, and their bid for the 2036 Olympic Games."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch some of Michael Chopra’s best goals for clubs including Newcastle, Sunderland and Cardiff City

Sky Sports News has followed the story of Indian-origin British footballers trying to play for India for more than a decade.

In 2014, former Newcastle striker Michael Chopra told Sky Sports News he was ready to play for India and that cricket great Sachin Tendulkar was ready to help him fulfil that desire.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former Wolves' capain Danny Batth is half-Indian and told Sky Sports News in 2017 that would love to play for India

In 2017, Danny Batth, who has just signed for Millwall and whose father was in born in Punjab, told Sky Sports News senior correspondent Rob Dorsett about his desire to play for India.

West Ham chief Virani targets Premier League return

West Ham interim chief executive officer Karim Virani wants the club to continue driving positive change, but admits the main goal is to make an immediate return to the Premier League.

The Hammers beat Leeds United in their final game last season, but it wasn't enough to prevent them from finishing 18th and suffering relegation.

"As we look ahead to the new [league] season, it's less than a week now and we have our first match, which has come around incredibly quickly," Virani said.

"The strength of the West Ham family in terms of supporting our team is going to be so crucial to our objectives as a football club - and everyone is aware we have one primary objective this year, which is to get out of the Championship and back to the Premier League.

Image: West Ham CEO Karim Virani in conversation with Sky Sports News' Dev Trehan (Photo: Vijay Bedesha)

"While it becomes very easy to quickly focus on the football, we should never forget the responsibility we have as a football club to drive positive action and impact off the pitch too.

"Personally I'm incredibly passionate about West Ham being at the forefront of championing equality and celebrating inclusion, and ensuring all of our matches - men's, women's and academy - are environments where everyone feels welcome."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kevin Nolan and Darren Moore tell the EFL show why Jarrod Bowen is key for West Ham's hopes for an instant return to the Premier League.

Virani was speaking at a West Ham United and Inclusive Irons event with Desi Ballers to close South Asian Heritage Month.

The event - also attended by club ambassadors Matt Jarvis and Bobby Seagull - shone a light on West Ham's work in the community.

Dhanda's dream debut

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Yan Dhanda recalls his Swansea debut in 2018 where he scored 30 seconds after coming on against Sheffield United with his very first touch in professional football.

The EFL kicks off again on Friday, presenting the perfect opportunity to look back at one of my favourite Championship moments, which happened eight years ago on the opening weekend of the season.

We often hear about dream debuts in football, but it's fair to say Yan Dhanda's first appearance for Swansea - and indeed his first taste of senior professional senior football - was exactly the stuff that dreams are made of.

It was a sunny afternoon at Brammall Lane, with the game locked at 1-1 in the closing stages of Graham Potter's first game as Swansea boss, away at Sheffield United.

Nobody, not even Dhanda, could have imagined what would happen next.

"It was crazy. I'd done really well in pre-season. I was only 19 but I was confident. I wanted to play. We got to Sheffield and I knew I was on the bench," Dhanda told me for Sky Sports News in 2018.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch all the angles! Yan Dhanda scored directly from a corner against Hibernian during his time as a Ross County player

"All night I'd been dreaming of coming on and scoring. I was texting my cousin the night before and saying imagine if I come on and score on my debut. It's the dream.

"I went to sleep and kept waking up. It was the first time I've ever been in a pro game. All I could think was coming on and scoring.

"Come the game, I was on the bench for the first time in a professional game. It's the Championship, I'm sitting there thinking this is fast, this is harder than I thought.

Image: Yan Dhanda is now at Hearts

"It was late in the game when Graham Potter told me I was coming on and I was buzzing - 30 seconds later, the ball fell to me in a good position where I backed myself.

"I just hit it and then it was a mad blur. My dad and cousin were in the stands right behind that goal. It was honestly the best feeling."
