Sports.title: 'He'll be a big player for us this season': What's next for Brian Madjo, Aston Villa's great young hope - TOM COLLOMOSSE reveals 17-year-old in line to start season opener, why Unai Emery is perfect for him and what PSG goal means for England future
Sports.content:
'He'll be a big player for us this season': What's next for Brian Madjo, Aston Villa's great young hope - TOM COLLOMOSSE reveals 17-year-old in line to start season opener, why Unai Emery is perfect for him and what PSG goal means for England future

Unlock more from Tom Collomosse inside the Villa camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Brian Madjo needed only 17 minutes to change Aston Villa’s outlook for the forthcoming season.

In that time he bullied Willian Pacho, one of the best markers in the world, and gave Marquinhos a fright, too. He had six attempts on goal and scored perhaps the most difficult, a far-post volley after outmuscling Pacho. Against Paris Saint-Germain, that would be a fair night’s work for any centre forward. For a 17-year-old making his competitive debut, it made the world sit up and take notice.

Even though they won the Super Cup, PSG were some way short of peak condition. Yet PSG are still PSG. For Madjo to make an impression like that was highly impressive and Daily Mail Sport understands he is leading the race to start the Premier League opener at Brighton on August 23, with Ollie Watkins not due back with the squad until this weekend.

Yet Madjo and fellow youngster George Hemmings, who was perhaps even more impressive, have lifted the mood around Villa Park.

Though supporters trust Unai Emery completely, they are frustrated at UEFA financial rules that have effectively forced them to sell Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne.

With Ezri Konsa also a target for Arsenal and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins returning to training only this weekend, there was creeping apprehension among some sections of the fanbase. For one night in Salzburg, Madjo’s performance blew that away.

Brian Madjo needed only 17 minutes to change Aston Villa’s outlook for the forthcoming season

He shrugged off the Paris Saint-Germain backline to fire in a euphoric equaliser for Aston Villa in the Super Cup on Wednesday night

What do his team-mates think?

Madjo joined Villa for £10million in January but his registration was initially blocked. The teenager is a Luxembourg international and FIFA’s regulations forbid overseas transfers of players under 18.

Yet Villa got the ruling overturned on appeal and Madjo, born in Enfield, north London, was cleared to play for them earlier this summer. Skipper John McGinn posted ‘English player allowed to play in England #freemadjo’ on his Instagram account – a sign of how well respected Madjo has become among the first-team squad.

‘He has obviously had to be very patient until he could play,’ said Tyrone Mings. ‘So, I think that says a lot about his character. He is very young and very strong. Clearly, mentally he is able to deal with setbacks.

‘He's a tough person to defend against. I think he is about 100kg (15st 11lb). He is a big old boy! He has got a very high ceiling. He is very difficult to play against.

‘He has trained with us for a long time. So when he eventually got his chance to play, he was ready. He knew our system, he knew how to press. I presume he watched a lot of Ollie Watkins and understood how we play. I’ve had a few chats with him in terms of what he’s about to go into.

‘The manager is big on what we do off the ball, probably more than what we do on the ball. Ollie’s a great person to watch, because of his work-rate and what he brings to the team.’

McGinn added: ‘He (Madjo) has been through a lot. He's not been able to play for six months to a year and he's handled that amazingly. He's kept himself in good shape. It would have been very easy for him to put his head down after those missed chances, but good strikers get themselves in those positions, and he's going to be a big player for us this season.’

He bullied Willian Pacho, one of the best markers in the world, and gave Marquinhos a fright, too, in the course of having six attempts on goal

Madjo scored twice in the first game of pre-season, a 5-0 win at Walsall last month, and also found the net against Real Sociedad and the Indonesia All Stars

Along with George Hemmings (pictured), who was perhaps even more impressive against PSG, Madjo has significantly raised the mood for Villa fans heading into the new season

What happens next?

Spotting the potential in Madjo and Hemmings, Emery deliberately loaded Villa’s pre-season schedule with fixtures. PSG were their seventh opponents of the summer programme, which Villa will complete against Borussia Monchengladbach on Saturday.

Emery wanted his younger players to grow accustomed to his style and tactical demands and on the evidence of the Super Cup, he was spot on.

Madjo has now scored five times in pre-season, with a brace against Walsall in the first friendly before also finding the net against Real Sociedad and the Indonesia All Stars.

Madjo’s rise makes it even likelier that Villa will listen to offers for Tammy Abraham between now and September 1, even though they paid £18million for the former England striker only seven months ago.

Daily Mail Sport understands Villa continue to track Nicolas Jackson and could still move in the closing hours of the window, though perhaps Madjo’s displays will make Emery wonder whether he needs two more forwards to compete with the 17-year-old.

Daily Mail Sport understands Madjo is leading the race to start the Premier League opener at Brighton on August 23

Even though he has represented Luxembourg three times, they were only friendlies, meaning Madjo is clear to play for England, for whom he has nine caps at Under-17 level

Even though he has represented Luxembourg three times, they were only friendlies, meaning Madjo is clear to play for England, for whom he has nine caps at Under-17 level. Expect him to be chosen for the forthcoming age-group squads.

He is remarkably strong for his age and loves a physical duel. Yet – quite understandably – there is work to do, particularly on his touch. The good news is that Emery has an outstanding track record of improving strikers and Madjo could not be in better hands.

As he prepares his team to meet Villa, you suspect Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler will hurriedly be making plans to contain this hugely exciting teenager.

Sports.title: Revealed: What Diego Simeone told Julian Alvarez in showdown talks after Arsenal target reiterated his desire to leave Atletico Madrid
Sports.content:
Revealed: What Diego Simeone told Julian Alvarez in showdown talks after Arsenal target reiterated his desire to leave Atletico Madrid

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Julian Alvarez has spoken to Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone for the first time since declaring that he wants to leave the club in order to 'fulfil my dream'.

The highly coveted Argentina forward, 26, is being tracked by several of Europe's biggest clubs, including Premier League champions Arsenal, LaLiga champions Barcelona and Real Madrid.

While representing Argentina at this summer's World Cup, Alvarez publicly declared his desire to leave Atletico, saying: 'I try to be an honest person. I spoke with the people at Atletico Madrid, and I think the best thing for everyone is a transfer. I want to fulfill my dream.'

Although reports have suggested Barcelona are Alvarez's preferred destination, Atletico have remained steadfast in their position that he is not for sale. Chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin said last month that the club would not entertain any offers for the striker, even in the region of £170m (€200 million).

Alvarez has a £428m (€500m) release clause and Atletico have already rejected a £129m (€150m) bid from Real Madrid.

The striker returned to pre-season training this week and, ahead of Wednesday's session, reportedly spent around 10 minutes speaking with Simeone at Atletico's Cerro del Espino training complex.

The striker returned to pre-season training this week after publicly declaring he would like to leave the club this summer in order to 'fulfil my dream'

Alvarez reportedly spent around 10 minutes speaking with Simeone (above) at Atletico's Cerro del Espino training complex, and reiterated his desire to leave during the conversation

According to reports, Alvarez, who is nicknamed La Arana, or 'The Spider', because of his Spider-Man celebration, reiterated his desire to leave during the conversation.

In response, Simeone is said to have restated the position he outlined publicly last week, namely that Atletico are planning for Alvarez to remain at the club.

'The situation is very clear, the club made a decision that Miguel Angel explained very well,' Simeone said. 'We are very happy with Julian. From a sporting perspective, we will help him to continue growing, to continue improving, and to give us back what he has given us in these two years, which was a great deal.'

The former Manchester City player, who won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina, joined Atletico in an £81.5m deal in 2024. He recorded 20 goals and nine assists in all competitions last season, while his 10 Champions League goals left him behind only Mbappe and Harry Kane in the scoring charts.

Back in April, Simeone said: 'I am not in Julian Alvarez's head. I suppose it is normal that an extraordinary player like Julian is wanted by Arsenal, Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona. It's normal because he's very good.'

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, meanwhile, has admitted there are 'very few players' in world football capable of immediately improving his starting XI, but insists the Gunners are still trying to make another marquee signing this summer.

Arsenal were heavily linked with Vinicius Jr before he signed a new contract with Real Madrid. They have, however, already secured the signing of Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes for £75m.

The former Manchester City player, who won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina, joined Atletico in an £81.5m deal in 2024

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, meanwhile, has insisted that the Gunners are still trying to make another marquee signing this summer

'I think for the margins to improve, there are very few players in the market that are available to do that and bring that to the club,' Arteta said after Arsenal's 1-1 draw with Como on Wednesday.

'Every time we have an opportunity to improve the squad and bring more quality and depth to the squad, we need to do that,' he said. 'We are actively trying to do so. The thing in the market is that it doesn't just depend on you. We are very clear on that.'

With more than two weeks remaining in the transfer window, there is still plenty of time for the situation to develop, while Arsenal may also benefit from Atletico's strained relationship with their LaLiga rivals.

One example came in June after Atletico rejected Real Madrid's £129m offer for Alvarez.

Real released a statement saying: 'Following the meeting of the board of directors held today, it has made an offer of 150 million euros to Club Atletico de Madrid for the federative rights of the player Julian Alvarez.

'After reviewing and evaluating the offer, Club Atletico de Madrid has expressed its gratitude for the proposal, made within the framework of the good relations between both clubs, and has rejected it, referring to the player's release clause.'

Atletico quoted the statement on X alongside a series of laughing emojis.

In a follow-up post, they added: 'You must have confused education with gratitude, but to leave no doubt: we don't thank you for anything.

'We neither study nor consider any offer for Julian. How could we not get along, when you make us laugh even more than Barcelona does.'

In a final swipe, Atletico posted: 'P.S. Taking advantage of the good relationship with your new president, let's see if you stop 'stealing' players from our Academy. Thanks a lot, @realmadrid!'

Sports.title: 'Hopefully I'm on a plane to Vegas and I've scored 507 goals!': Josh Windass on Wrexham's Premier League dream, Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac - and the 'magic spell' behind Phil Parkinson's incredible tenure
Sports.content:
'Hopefully I'm on a plane to Vegas and I've scored 507 goals!': Josh Windass on Wrexham's Premier League dream, Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac - and the 'magic spell' behind Phil Parkinson's incredible tenure

Unlock more of the best of our football coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Josh Windass is not your stereotypical footballer.

Refreshingly honest, the forward, son of cult hero Dean, doesn’t celebrate when he scores – insisting ‘I just don’t get happy’ – and admitted his American in-laws knew more about Wrexham than him when he joined the club last summer.

For most players, a calf injury that meant they were unable to play a part in Wrexham’s pre-season tour of the US would have been enough to get them down.

But not Windass.

‘We’ve been on tour in America,’ he tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘So it’s just been brilliant for me. I’ve been on holiday for two weeks, doing my rehab in the sun!

‘It is frustrating not to be playing but I’m not one for pre-season games. I think they’re all nonsense. Whether you win or lose, the proof will be in the pudding.’

Wrexham No 10 Josh Windass is hoping to lead Phil Parkinson's side to the Premier League

Windass scored 16 goals and provided five assists in just 28 league starts last season

Windass’ dry humour shines through during our conversation and despite his setback, he hopes to be fit for Wrexham’s Championship opener against Cardiff – if not their second game with Watford.

It would be a shame for him to have to wait much longer after he enjoyed one of the best seasons of his career last term.

Having departed Sheffield Wednesday on the eve of the campaign amid their financial turmoil, Windass scored 16 goals and provided five assists in just 28 league starts.

The No 10 was one of 13 summer arrivals as Wrexham endured an inevitable adaptation period following three successive promotions.

But, over the winter, Phil Parkinson's side climbed the table and ultimately missed out on the play-offs in heartbreaking fashion on the final day after drawing with Middlesbrough.

‘I was disappointed we didn’t make the play-offs as that was our aim,’ Windass says. ‘But I try and do as best as I can and, as a No 10, you want to score and set up goals.

‘From Christmas onwards we were one of the top three or four teams in the league and, once you've got the proof you can do it (it’s massive). If we'd have done that all season, we'd have had a good chance of promotion.'

Windass has played for some big clubs in his career, including Rangers, but insists nothing compares to what he has experienced at Wrexham over the past 12 months.

'It is the best culture I've ever been in by a country mile,' says Windass of Wrexham's dressing room

‘I don't know how he (Phil Parkinson) does it, because every club I've been at, you always have a few people you sign who are not great (personalities)'

‘It's honestly incredible,’ he adds. ‘Before you get there, everyone says, “Oh, it's the best dressing room ever, the culture's amazing”. And you're like, yeah, sure it is.

‘But it is the best dressing room and culture I've ever been in by a country mile. What the gaffer, Ryan (Reynolds) and Rob (Mac) have created with everybody, how they get on with each other – in football you generally don't get that in changing rooms. Here it's different.'

Parkinson doesn’t get the credit he deserves for what has been a transformative five-year spell in North Wales.

He is now the fourth longest-serving manager in English football and, despite significant turnover in the playing squad, he has remained throughout Wrexham’s evolution from a struggling non-League side into one of the most marketable clubs in the world.

So, what's the secret?

‘He's had so much success,’ Windass says. ‘The way he recruits players for the dressing room, not just for the style of play (is amazing).

‘I don't think he's made a bad signing in terms of that. He does his due diligence with character references. He signs good players, but ultimately he signs boys who want to fight for each other and get on, both on and off the pitch.

‘I don't know how he does it, because every club I've been at, you always have a few people you sign who are not great for the dressing room.

‘But at Wrexham it's like he's got a magic spell because everyone comes in and is top class.’

On Wrexham's Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac, Windass adds: 'They’re the same with every player. They speak to us all the time and we're just a reflection of them. They're winners and the club has shown that in the last five years.’

Windass is full of praise for Wrexham's Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds (left) and Rob Mac

Sunderland goalkeeper Anthony Patterson is expected to boost Wrexham's promotion bid

As Wrexham have risen through the leagues, each summer has been accompanied by significant change in the squad.

Yet, with Parkinson’s side set to play a second campaign in the same division for the first time since their promotion from the National League, this has been one of continuity.

Crystal Palace full back Danny Imray, who shone on loan at West Brom last season, and Preston captain Ben Whiteman are the only players through the door, although more arrivals are expected – including Sunderland goalkeeper Anthony Patterson. Steve Nickson also joined from Newcastle as director of football.

And Windass believes a more settled squad could prove to be a significant benefit to Wrexham, although he admits they must improve defensively after they shipped more goals than relegated Oxford last season.

‘That’s the nail on the head,’ he adds. ‘I don't think people realise how many new players we had on the pitch last year, and maybe that's why it took until Christmas for us to gel and start playing well.

‘We've got 98 per cent of the team still here, we're all used to playing with each other and we get on great. The new signings have settled in seamlessly, so we're going to have a good chance.’

As our conversation comes to a close, Windass’ wit is on display again when asked what a dream campaign would look like if we were talking again at the end of the season.

‘Hopefully, I'm on a plane to Vegas having just won promotion,’ he says. 'And I've scored 20… no, I’ve scored 507 goals!’

Sports.title: BBC commentator can’t hide frustration over fall drama as Keely Hodgkinson rival escapes
Sports.content:
BBC commentator can’t hide frustration over fall drama as Keely Hodgkinson rival escapes

BBC Sport commentator Steve Cram has criticised European Championships referees after Swiss runner Audrey Werro was awarded a place in the 800m final following an appeal

View 2 Images Audrey Werro fell during her 800m semi-final at the European Championship. (Image: BBC Sport)

BBC Sport commentator Steve Cram has criticised the European Championship officials prior to Audrey Werro being handed a spot in the 800m final following an investigation. The Swiss runner seemed to trip themselves up as they neared the final straight in their 800m semi-final, finishing in last place, but Keely Hodgkinson's rival was given a reprieve.

‌



Werro tumbled to the track while going round the final bend, before getting back to her feet, and completing the race. BBC footage appeared to show the 22-year-old clipping her own leg before going down, admitting she would challenge the outcome.

‌



Upon further examination, Anais Bourgoin disrupted the Swiss athlete's rhythm with a slight touch on Werro's foot with her left hand, causing her to fall to the ground.

‌



European Championship drama as Keely Hodgkinson's main rival wins appeal despite BBC footage READ MORE :

Keely Hodgkinson shows her true colours in BBC interview as result changed after appeal READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Nevertheless, BBC commentator Cram took a different view and said: "Look, she tripped herself, that's reasonably evident. But look, we all want to see the best athletes in the final, even Keely said that..

"Referees have had a look at it, Galvydyt definitely should have been advanced as it wasn't her fault she tripped. Yes the push and shove of 800m running, these sort of things happen.

‌



"I think the question marks now are going to be I don't think Great Britain are going to counter-protest this, as I said Keely wants her to be there.

View 2 Images Audrey Werro fell during the 800m semi-final. (Image: BBC Sport)

"The question probably is is Verro okay, that was a hard fall, she seemed to be okay, but it's also psychologically coming away from that, coming back tomorrow night, don't have time to really process it that much.

‌



"But she's in, 10 in the final, it's going to be tough, it's going to change the way the race would have been run.

"Keely would have had one plan for Femke (Broeders-Bol), there was only Femke, but now she's going to go back to thinking about both of them, and that's going to obviously be a challenge. But we're getting the final that we wanted, that's the way to look at it."

The reprieve means Werro will go head-to-head with Hodgkinson in the 800m final tomorrow. The Atherton born runner showed her class after winning her own semi-final to book her place in the final.

Article continues below

"I heard an ‘oooh’ which is never a good sign," Hodgkinson said in an interview with the BBC. "But I don’t know what it looked like.

"Obviously it’s a real shame. I hope she’s okay and I hope she’s in the final tomorrow, that would be a really exciting race. All round, happy for myself to go through."

Sports.title: Man Utd star Youri Tielemans issues grovelling apology over comments in interview
Sports.content:
Man Utd star Youri Tielemans issues grovelling apology over comments in interview

Manchester United summer arrival Youri Tielemans has been forced to apologise after his comments following the cross Premier League move

View 2 Images Youri Tielemans joined Man United in the summer. (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United midfielder Youri Tielemans has been forced to apologise following his comments after leaving Aston Villa. The summer arrival claimed that the Red Devils were above his former employers, whom he helped back to European silverware with their Europa League triumph.

‌



The Red Devils made the move for the 29-year-old during the summer as they triggered the £35million release clause within his contract. Tielemans ended his three year spell in the West Midlands and arrived as part of the reinforcements in Michael Carrick's midfield, a problem position at Old Trafford in recent years.

‌



However, Tielemans sparked anger with his comments in his first extended sit-down with journalists as the conclusion to United's pre-season preparations looms closer.

‌



Wayne Rooney lands new Man Utd gig alongside Mark Goldbridge for Gary Neville's Overlap READ MORE :

Michael Carrick provides Marcus Rashford transfer update with telling Man Utd statement READ MORE :

In a post to Instagram, he said: "Never meant for my words in the press yesterday to offend anyone or undermine the institution of Aston Villa Football Club which I massively respect and I'm grateful to for the past three years.

"I must however admit my mistake and apologise for my choice of words, (I) will be more careful in the future. Wishing the club the best in the future. Youri."

Factions of the Villa Park faithful appear to have taken umbrage with the comments made by the Belgium captain. Tielemans said: "I am very thankful to Aston Villa. I owe them the world.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"It is a great club, we did amazing things, and they have put me back to my best level. But there are clubs above Villa, and Manchester United is one of them.

"It is a great achievement for any footballer to end up here. It means you have done well in your career. But it does not end there. I want to be successful."

‌



Tielemans has featured prominently during the preparations for the new season, which begin on August 22 with a trip to newly promoted Hull City.

View 2 Images Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have joined United this summer (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

United's final game of their pre-season build-up comes against AC Milan, managed by Ruben Amorim who was sacked by the Red Devils in January.

‌



United have been busy in the window, acquiring Andrey Santos to help bolster their midfield, while work remains ongoing to further strengthen positions across the pitch.

It is an important season for Carrick and his side as they return to the Champions League following last season's third-place finish. All eyes will be on whether they can compete on all fronts, however, on the pitch the focus will be on alleviating the burden on Bruno Fernandes.

The United captain has been instrumental for the club during a dour period in the club's history. Tielemans has already talked up the relationship with his midfield partner.

He said: "It's really natural. He is a guy that can find space easily. I just try and find him so that he can move forward."

Sports.title: Jockey Katie Davis flies off rearing horse into the crowd in scary moment at Saratoga
Sports.content:
Jockey Katie Davis flies off rearing horse into the crowd in scary moment at Saratoga

The popular US rider escaped without injury after the incident which occurred as she was heading to the New York track on Free Spin Kim

View 2 Images Katie Davis aboard her unruly mount before heading into the crowd

Popular US jockey Katie Davis escaped injury after she flew into the crowd from an unruly horse.

‌



Davis, who took part in last year’s Shergar Cup at Ascot, was heading out onto the track on three-year-old filly Free Spin Kim for the third race at Saratoga in New York State on Wednesday.

‌



Free Spin Kim, who was unplaced in two previous starts, was following the outrider when she suddenly reared and backed into a rail alongside the walkway. Davis flew off the horse and over the rail into the watching crowd and disappeared from view. She was later seen back on her feet talking to connections of the filly, appearing none the worse for the incident. Free Spin Kim was scratched from the maiden claiming race by a vet, declared injured.

‌



Max Comley thrilled to get the nod to train first jumps horse for owners Amo Racing READ MORE :

Reviewing the incident, Fox Sports pundit, former jockey Richard Migliore said Free Spin Kim “reared up, went backwards into the rail.

“And as a rider at that point you’ve got to hit the eject button. You don’t want to ride that ship down to the ground, you’ve got to get away from them.

“She kind of got launched out to the crowd. She looks like she’s no worse for the wear.”

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Among comments from fans on social media, one commented, “I’m glad you weren’t seriously injured Katie. That was scary to watch and I’m sure it was even more so for you.”

Another said: “Dang that was quite a toss, glad she’s okay.”

‌



View 2 Images Katie Davis: rode at last year's Shergar Cup (Image: Courtesy of John Hoy)

While Colleen Phelan wrote on her X account: “Fun fact @jockeykdavis flew into me and my mom. She 100% is the reason that horse didn’t go through the fence. What a legend.”

The 34-year-old Davis is from a family of jockeys. Her father, sister and brother are all past and currently successful riders. She has ridden 365 winners.

She made her British debut in 2025 when she represented the Rest Of The World at the Shergar Cup.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino losing grip on FIFA as Ireland's FA release statement in another blow
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino losing grip on FIFA as Ireland's FA release statement in another blow

Pressure is continuing to mount on Gianni Infantino's shoulders following controversial FIFA decisions

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino has come under fire in recent months (Image: PA Wire)

Gianni Infantino's grip on the FIFA presidency continues to loosen as yet another footballing body has released a statement criticising the president. The Irish FA has released a statement rescinding its letter of support for Infantino and explained the reason for doing so.

‌



A statement from the FAI on Thursday morning read: "Following an FAI Board Meeting, the decision was taken to rescind the letter of support that the Association supplied earlier this year. It has since written to Fifa to explain its reasoning.

‌



"The Association is grateful for the support that Fifa provides to Irish football, but recent events have raised significant concerns regarding governance, transparency and the lack of meaningful consultation.

‌



"Considering the governance challenges that the FAI has had to overcome in recent years, the Association feels a particular obligation to advocate for and uphold best practice."

Gianni Infantino eyes another huge World Cup change to secure position as FIFA chief READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Last week the Welsh FA became the first of the home nations governing bodies to withdraw their support for Infantino, with the English FA following suit. It follows on from the FIFA president's brazen attempt to sell stakes in the company's commercial operations to private investors - which would impact the World Cup.

‌



UEFA, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation accused Infantino of breaking trust 'through deception' in an open letter published on Monday. Northern Ireland's IFA have noted the "wider concerns" raised by those in football regarding Infantino, but has not gone as far as withdrawing it's support of Infantino, though did support UEFA's stance.

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has come under criticism (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

"We take our responsibilities as a member association of both Uefa and Fifa seriously," said an IFA spokesperson.

‌



"We support the current Uefa position on the matter and will continue to engage constructively on issues relating to football governance.

"We are of course aware of the recent developments and wider concerns within the football community. We are considering these matters carefully and will continue to engage through the appropriate governance structures and channels.

"At this stage, we have no further comment."

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard's call to Virgil van Dijk that saw Liverpool win Man City transfer battle
Sports.content:
Steven Gerrard's call to Virgil van Dijk that saw Liverpool win Man City transfer battle

Virgil van Dijk was the subject of a transfer tug-of-war involving Liverpool and Manchester City with a phone call from Steven Gerrard proving key

View 2 Images Liverpool signed Virgil van Dijk despite interest from Man City

Steven Gerrard has recalled a phone call he received from Virgil van Dijk when he was being pursued by Liverpool and Manchester City where he delivered a blunt message to the defender.

‌



Van Dijk had established himself as one of the Premier League's best centre-halves and made it known to Southampton that he wanted to move on. A summer move failed to materialise, but the saga was always going to continue come January.

‌



Liverpool would win the race, spending a then club-record £75million to land Van Dijk, who made an instant impact as he helped the Reds make the Champions League final within months of joining.

‌



Gerrard recalls Van Dijk phoning him to so that he could get a greater impression of the Merseyside outfit. The Dutchman wasn't looking for the Liverpool legend to sell him the club, instead seeking a greater insight, but Gerrard did make it clear that Liverpool's traditions far exceeded City's.

The former midfielder recalled during Captains, a new LFC Original: “He phoned me at the time actually. I knew his agent really well. It was City, Liverpool.

“He said to me, ‘I haven’t phoned you to sort of push me one way or the other, because I know which way you’re going to push me. But just tell me a little bit about Liverpool?’

‌



“I just said to him, ‘Look, if it’s about what the clubs stand for and what the clubs are about, you’re wasting your time because I think you already know the answer to that.’ It was an interesting conversation and I was so happy that he chose us.”

View 2 Images Virgil van Dijk scored on debut for Liverpool back in 2018 (Image: Getty Images)

Van Dijk would enjoy the dream debut, scoring against Everton to knock them out of the FA Cup and concedes he was determined to wear red. “That feeling of, like, I wanted to play for this club so badly, it was so intense," he said. "And the fans embraced me from day one. Scoring also against Everton [on his debut] helped massively too!”

Article continues below

Within 18 months of signing Van Dijk had been named the PFA Player of the Year and proved crucial in Liverpool's Champions League success of 2019. The following year he helped the Reds' end their 30-year wait for a top flight title. Van Dijk remains Liverpool's defensive leader despite turning 35 this summer.

Sports.title: Keely Hodgkinson shows her true colours in BBC interview as result changed after appeal
Sports.content:
Keely Hodgkinson shows her true colours in BBC interview as result changed after appeal

Keely Hodgkinson sent a classy message to Audrey Werro after her 800m rival suffered a fall during the European Championship semi-finals

View 2 Images Keely Hodgkinson gave an interview after her 800m rival Audrey Werro suffered a nasty fall (Image: BBC)

Keely Hodgkinson sent her best wishes to Audrey Werro after her rival sustained a nasty fall at the European Championships. Werro was leading the first 800m semi-final before suddenly falling with less than 200m to go, but it has since been confirmed that she will compete in the final following a successful appeal.

‌



Replays on the BBC appeared to show that Werro tripped over her own leg before falling. There was an investigation into whether or not the Swiss runner would be able to feature in Friday’s final, which has now been confirmed will be the case.

‌



Hodgkinson went on to win the second semi-final, and was asked for her thoughts on the fall from Werro, which happened a few minutes before the start of her race.

‌



“I heard an ‘oooh’ which is never a good sign,” Hodgkinson said in an interview with the BBC. “But I don’t know what it looked like.”

European Championship drama as Keely Hodgkinson's main rival wins appeal despite BBC footage READ MORE :

Keely Hodgkinson shows true colours as she speaks out about what athletics has cost her READ MORE :

When asked if seeing the fall would have changed her approach to the race, Hodgkinson added: “No not at all. You can’t worry about what other people are doing or what happens to them."

Showing her true class, Hodgkinson continued: “Obviously it’s a real shame. I hope she’s okay and I hope she’s in the final tomorrow, that would be a really exciting race. All round, happy for myself to go through.”

‌



The BBC confirmed that Werro and fellow faller Gabija Galvydyte will be in the final, meaning there will be 10 athletes running for gold tomorrow evening.

Werro opened up on her fall in the semi-final and confirmed her intention to appeal the decision, which has now been successful.

“I was feeling really great until the last moment but unfortunately something happened and I was on the ground one second after,” Werro told the BBC.

‌



“I hope I’ll be qualified for the final, I hope I’ll be able to go (to the final).”

View 2 Images Keely Hodgkinson (Image: Mike Egerton/PA Wire)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Werro added: “Yes, this is the reason why. I finished the race and it’s always important to go until the end. Now we will see what happens.”

Hodgkinson ran a 1:57 to win the second 800m semi-final and advance to Friday’s final, and the 24-year-old went on to be quizzed on what she wanted from the race.

“Nothing really, just to get through. I think it was a similar race to the heats because the depth is so good,” she said.

‌



“Another 1:57. Overall I’m happy and can’t complain.”

Hodgkinson added: “Yeah, the excitement makes me excited. I can’t wait to step out there. I love a good challenge, I think it brings out the best in me.

“Hopefully it’ll be a really good race and a clean race with no-one falling over tomorrow!”

‌

BBC commentator Steve Cram went on to say during the post-race analysis: "Look, she [Werro] tripped herself, that's reasonably evident. But look, we all want to see the best athletes in the final, even Keely said that.

“Referees have had a look at it, Galvydyte definitely should have been advanced as it wasn't her fault she tripped. Yes the push and shove of 800m running, these sort of things happen.

‌



“I think the question marks now are going to be, I don't think Great Britain are going to counter-protest this, as I said Keely wants her to be there.

“The question probably is is Verro okay, that was a hard fall, she seemed to be okay, but it's also psychologically coming away from that, coming back tomorrow night, don't have time to really process it that much.

“But she's in, 10 in the final, it's going to be tough, it's going to change the way the race would have been run.

“Keely would have had one plan for Femke (Broeders-Bol), there was only Femke, but now she's going to go back to thinking about both of them, and that's going to obviously be a challenge. But we're getting the final that we wanted, that's the way to look at it."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
